title: Karunanidhi and Jayalalithaa: Clashes of Two Titans
summary: When Jayalalithaa launched blistering attacks in fluent English, Karunanidhi disarmed the house with unmatched Tamil wit, listing concrete welfare reforms with poetic grace.
keywords: Karunanidhi and Jayalalithaa: Clashes of Two Titans
full_text:
For nearly three decades—from 1989 to 2016—Tamil Nadu politics was defined by the titanic duel between M. Karunanidhi and J. Jayalalithaa.

Both were towering figures with fanatical followings. Jayalalithaa possessed formidable command over English and an imperious, unyielding presence; Karunanidhi wielded classical Tamil with unparalleled rhetorical finesse.

Whenever they locked horns in the Assembly, the atmosphere was supercharged.

During one memorable budget session, Opposition Leader Jayalalithaa launched a blistering offensive:
"Chief Minister Karunanidhi is presiding over a totally corrupt, rudderless, and incompetent administration! This government has forfeited every moral right to govern for another hour!"

DMK benches erupted in fury, but Karunanidhi raised his hand, gesturing for calm.

Adjusting his glasses, he smiled with gentle irony and addressed the Speaker:
"Mr. Speaker, Sir! The Honorable Leader of the Opposition has delivered a furious sermon in magnificent English.
I admire her flawless English pronunciation. Alas, the only thing missing from her eloquence is a single grain of truth!
The Madam brands us 'Incompetent'!
If we are incompetent... who provided free electricity to the suffering farmers of Tamil Nadu?
Who enacted the historic law granting equal property rights to women?
Who introduced rice at one rupee per kilogram for the poorest families?

The Madam issues fiery statements in English from an air-conditioned palace; we sit in the huts of the poor and wipe their tears in Tamil!
She is welcome to display her fury in the English language; but the ordinary people will vote for us in Tamil!"

The chamber erupted in thunderous ovation.

Karunanidhi disarmed fierce aggression not with counter-insults, but with a record of progressive welfare policies articulated through literary wit.
moral: Aggression and rhetoric are easily demolished when countered by calm dignity and genuine achievements for the common good.
